newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major appeals to voters to trust him.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major appeals to voters to trust him.

text.p: John Major put the question of trust back at the heart of Britain's election on Wednesday with an impassioned appeal to voters to have faith in him.

Rallying his Conservative Party supporters in Aberdeen, Major attacked opposition Labour party leader Tony Blair as arrogant and untested and said his policies would sell out Britain in Europe and precipitate the breakup of the United Kingdom.

In prepared remarks to be given in a speech later on Wednesday, Major said, "I appeal to you don't let whatever doubts you may have had about the Conservative Party in the past weigh with you, when the future of the United Kingdom may be at stake."
"Think about it. Think seriously. Think again."
"Look in my eyes and know this. I will always deal fair and true by this great nation," Major said.
The appeal was an explicit recognition by Major that his personal popularity is his deeply divided party's best hope of winning an unprecedented fifth straight term in office.
"Like me or loathe me, on the issues I put before you today, you know where I stand."

Crystallising his attack on Labour, which enjoys a large but declining opinon poll lead, Major said Blair would be a soft touch on the great issues facing Britain because of his inexperience and lack of principle.

"Funded by the unions, instinctively integrationist, appeasing the (Scottish) separatists, Labour, led by Mr Blair, would destroy British prosperity, risk dividing Britain and put us on the escalator to a federal Europe," Major said.

"Our United Kingdom would be reduced to a country of regions. Our national parliament, the buttress of our democracy, would be sidelined. Divided, separated, weakened, we would become a pawn in a federal Europe," he added.

Major, who believes his fierce defence of Scotland's place in the UK helped him to come back from behind to win the 1992 election, accused Blair of showing a "whiff of arrogrance" in the high-handed way in which he has formulated Labour's Scottish policy.

Referring to Labour's plan to use purple as its campaign colour in the runup to polling day, Major said, "I see the Labour red changing an imperial purple -- and I see a man carried away by his own propaganda."
Major contrasted his negotiating skills in Europe with what he called Blair's declared willingess to surrender Britain's national interest.

"The federalist of Europe cannot believe their luck. Mr Blair has appeared. Talking of a fresh start in Europe. Talking of concessions in Europe. Talking of being 'constructive' in Europe -- that's Brussels speak for giving way," Mayor said.

Again bringing the six-week campaign down to a question of personalities, Major added "Can we risk such a man as our prime minister? He's given away some of Britain's best cards before the game has even begun."
Earlier on Wednesday, Major's Conservative were buoyed by a new poll showing they had slashed Labour's double digit lead to just five points.
The ICM poll in The Guardian newspaper showed Labour's lead down to five from 14, the first time the opposition's advantage has fallen to single figures since November 1993.
